spots.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
spots.summary: The Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum is a museum for the Cambodian genocide. Located in Phnom Penh, the site is a former secondary school that had been turned into an internment facility known as Security Prison 21 (S-21) by the Khmer Rouge regime from 1975 until its fall in 1979.

spots.name: Royal Palace
spots.summary: The Royal Palace of Cambodia is a complex of buildings which serves as the official royal residence of the King of Cambodia. Its full name in Khmer is the Preah Barom Reacheaveang Chaktomuk Serey Mongkol.

spots.name: Wat Phnom
spots.summary: Wat Phnom is a Buddhist temple (wat) in Doun Penh, Phnom Penh. The site features a pagoda, a stupa symbolizing the name of Phnom Penh, and a historical site that is part of the Khmer national identity. Wat Phnom has a total height of 46 meters (150 ft).

spots.name: National Museum of Cambodia
spots.summary: The National Museum of Cambodia is Cambodia's largest museum of cultural history and is the country's leading historical and archaeological museum. It is located in Chey Chumneas, Phnom Penh.

names.ja: プノンペン国立博物館

spots.name: Silver Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Silver Pagoda is located on the south side of the Royal Palace in Chey Chumneas, Phnom Penh. The official name is Wat Ubaosoth Ratanaram, also known as Wat Preah Keo Morakot which is commonly shortened to Wat Preah Keo in Khmer.

photo.author: Original uploader was User:Adam Carr at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Central Market
spots.summary: The Central Market is a market and an art deco landmark in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia. The bright yellow building completed in 1937 has a 26-metre high central dome, with four tall arch-roofed arms branching out diagonally across the block, creating vast hallways housing countless stalls and a variety of goods.

spots.name: Independence Monument
spots.summary: The Independence Monument in Phnom Penh, capital of Cambodia, was built in 1958 to memorialise Cambodia's independence from France in 1953. It stands on a roundabout in the intersection of Norodom Boulevard and Sihanouk Boulevard in the centre of the city.

spots.name: Cambodian Memorial Sites
spots.summary: The Cambodian Memorial Sites: From centres of repression to places of peace and reflection is a UNESCO World Heritage Site which consists of the former M-13 prison, the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center.

names.nl: Cambodjaanse gedenkplaatsen: Van centra van repressie tot plaatsen van vrede en bezinning
names.zh: 柬埔寨纪念遗址：从压迫中心到和平与反思之地

spots.name: Wat Ounalom
spots.summary: Wat Ounalom is a wat located on Sisowath Quay in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, near the Chaktomuk Royal Palace. As the former seat of Cambodia's Mahanikaya Order, it is regarded as the most important wat in Phnom Penh and the central institution of Cambodian Buddhism. It was established in 1443 and consists of 44 structures.

spots.name: Wat Botum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Botum, the official name is Wat Botum Vatey Reachavararam literally means "The temple of lotus which was built by the king", is a wat (pagoda) located on Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It is to the south of the Royal Palace on the western side of Wat Botum Park.

spots.name: Notre Dame Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Christ the King Cathedral, also known as the Cathedral of Phnom Penh, was a 19th-century French Gothic revival church that served as the cathedral of the Apostolic Vicariate of Phnom Penh. It was located in the Russei Keo District of the city on Monivong Boulevard.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Roman Catholic Cathedral of Phnom Penh

spots.name: Wat Langka

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Langka is a wat located in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It is one of the five ancient pagodas in Phnom Penh and was built in B.E. 1985. The temple was originally constructed as a place of refuge and for the safekeeping of the Tripiṭaka, as well as a meeting place for Khmer and Sri Lankan monks.

spots.name: Sisowath Quay
spots.summary: Sisowath Quay is a 3-kilometre riverfront strip along the Tonlé Sap River in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

spots.name: National Library of Cambodia

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Cambodia is the national library of Cambodia, based in Phnom Penh, created by France in 1924.

names.ja: カンボジア国立図書館

spots.name: Wat Saravan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Saravan, officially Wat Saravan Techo, is a wat in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It is located to the northwest of the Royal Palace of Cambodia and southwest of Wat Ounalom. It is said to have over 3,400 manuscripts in what has been described as the largest library in the country.

spots.name: Olympic Stadium
spots.summary: The National Olympic Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It has a capacity of 30,000. Despite its name, the stadium has never hosted an Olympic Games.

names.ja: プノンペン・オリンピックスタジアム

spots.name: Cambodia–Vietnam Friendship Monument
spots.summary: The Cambodia–Vietnam Friendship Monument in Phnom Penh, capital of Cambodia, is a large concrete monument commemorating the former alliance between Vietnam and Cambodia. It was built in 1979 by the communist regime that took power after the Cambodian-Vietnamese War, which overthrew the Khmer Rouge regime.

spots.name: Monivong Bridge
spots.summary: Monivong Bridge is a heavily trafficked bridge in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It bridges the Bassac River near the end of National Highway 2 to southern Cambodia and lies along the National Highway 1 which connects the city to eastern Cambodia and Vietnam.

spots.name: Al-Serkal

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Al-Serkal Mosque is the main mosque in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia.

names.ja: アルサークル・モスク

spots.name: Nur ul-Ihsan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nur ul-Ihsan Mosque was, until 2018, the oldest mosque in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia. It was situated 7 km north of the centre of the city.

spots.name: Sihanouk Boulevard
spots.summary: Sihanouk Boulevard is a central boulevard of Phnom Penh which is the capital of Cambodia. The boulevard crosses the city in an east–west direction. It is named in honour of the late King Norodom Sihanouk, one of the country's greatest kings.

spots.name: Freedom Park
spots.summary: Freedom Park, also known as Democracy Square, was a 8,000-square-kilometre (3,100 sq mi) plaza in downtown Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It was the site of a number of protests from the 1990s until the 2010s.

spots.name: RCAF Old Stadium
spots.summary: RCAF Stadium, also known as the Old Stadium or Lambert Stadium, is a stadium in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It has a capacity of 8,000 spectators. It is the home stadium of Royal Cambodian Armed Forces FC of the Cambodian League. The stadium also hosts matches of the Cambodia national football team.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This lady serves inexpensive and super delicious local curries with noodles and an immense portion of meat at an unbeatable price. The only catch is that you either take-away or seat yourself onto one of the tiny chairs around her place, but without any table to put your bowl. However, the dish is definitely worth the trouble.

spots.summary: In the evenings at Sun & Moon Urban Hotel, guests and local residents can chill out in style at Cloud 9, the hotel’s rooftop bar, with cool beats, creative cocktails, and spectacular views over Phnom Penh city. Poolside BBQ parties and buffet dinners can also be arranged at this location.

spots.summary: The BBK1 area is experiencing great growth in construction and becoming continually more an upmarket area of the city. At the junction of St 51 and St 310, each corner now has a multinational joint, KFC, Burger King, Carl's Jnr (California flame grilled burgers) and Gloria Jean's coffee.

spots.summary: Tallest sky bar in Phnom Penh, is a hidden gem in the heart of the city’s business district. From the roof of the 22-story Hyundai Phnom Penh Tower, the view of the city is breath-taking, and the soft mix of pop music in the background adds to the bar’s relaxed ambiance.
